transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you that made you decide to come here today?

I guess… the main reason I came is that I don’t feel like myself anymore, especially around work. I used to think of myself as pretty capable — like, I was the person people trusted, I’d been promoted, I knew what I was doing. And now I keep having this feeling that work just isn’t safe anymore. Not in a logical checklist kind of way, exactly, but it feels unsafe in my body and in my head.

And it’s not just that. It’s like something in me changed, and I can’t convince myself it hasn’t. I keep thinking I’m damaged now, like the competent version of me that earned that promotion isn’t really there anymore, or maybe was never as solid as I thought. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it’s been hard to shake, and it’s starting to feel like I can’t just push through it the way I usually would.
Can you think of a specific event or change in your life that happened around the time these feelings started?

Yes. It started after the break-in during that overnight deployment at work. That’s the thing I keep coming back to, even though I sometimes try to tell myself it was “just one bad night” or that I should be over it by now.

It’s been… about two years and four months since then, which sounds weirdly specific, but I think I keep track because everything feels divided into before and after that night. Before the deployment, I was stressed, sure, but it was normal work stress. After the break-in, it was like something in me just didn’t reset properly. So yes, that’s the specific event — the break-in during that overnight deployment — and these feelings have basically been going on since then.
Since the break-in, have you had recurring and distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings related to that night?

Yes. I mean… yes, definitely. It doesn’t even always feel like a “memory” in the normal sense, like I’m calmly remembering something that happened. It’s more like something small happens and suddenly I’m back there before I can stop it.

Like if a badge scanner beeps in the wrong way, or if I hear heavy footsteps in the hallway at work, especially when it’s quiet, my body reacts before my brain catches up. A late-night deployment alert can do it too — that sound or that message coming in, and it’s like everything narrows. My chest gets tight, and I’m not just thinking about that night, I’m seeing parts of it again.

The image that comes back the most is the guard on the floor. It just cuts straight through whatever I’m doing. I can be looking at a screen or talking to someone, and then that image is there, really sharp, and for a moment it feels like I’m in that office again. I know I’m technically not, but it doesn’t feel that way right away. It’s distressing, and it’s… it’s exhausting, because it can come out of nowhere.
